PRENATAL GENETIC TESTING REPORT
[redacted location] Regional Genetics Laboratory

PATIENT INFORMATION
Patient Name: [redacted name]
Date of Birth: [redacted date]
Medical Record Number: [redacted ID]
Referring Physician: Dr. [redacted name]
Date of Collection: [redacted date]
Date of Report: [redacted date]

CLINICAL INDICATION
Prenatal testing following abnormal ultrasound findings

SPECIMEN TYPE
Chorionic villi (uncultured)

TEST PERFORMED
Quantitative Fluorescence Polymerase Chain Reaction (QF-PCR) for rapid aneuploidy detection

METHODOLOGY
QF-PCR analysis was performed on DNA extracted from uncultured chorionic villi to detect common aneuploidies. This test utilizes chromosome-specific short tandem repeat (STR) markers to assess copy number for chromosomes 13, 18, and 21. Multiple informative markers are analyzed for each chromosome to ensure diagnostic accuracy.

Markers analyzed:
- Chromosome 13: D13S631, D13S258, D13S742, D13S628
- Chromosome 18: D18S535, D18S391, D18S390, D18S386
- Chromosome 21: D21S1435 (21q21.3), D21S1411 (21q21.3), D21S1270 (21q22.3), D21S1437 (21q22.3)

RESULTS

Chromosome 21: ABNORMAL - Trisomy 21 detected
- D21S1435: Three alleles detected (peak ratio 1:1:1)
- D21S1411: Three alleles detected (peak ratio 1:1:1)
- D21S1270: Three alleles detected (peak ratio 1:1:1)
- D21S1437: Two alleles detected (peak ratio 2:1)

Chromosome 13: Normal disomic pattern
- All markers show expected biallelic patterns

Chromosome 18: Normal disomic pattern
- All markers show expected biallelic patterns

INTERPRETATION
The QF-PCR analysis demonstrates trisomy 21 (Down syndrome) in this fetal sample. Three informative markers for chromosome 21 show triallelic patterns consistent with the presence of three copies of chromosome 21. The findings for chromosomes 13 and 18 are consistent with a normal complement.

These molecular findings of trisomy 21 are consistent with the reported abnormal ultrasound findings and indicate Down syndrome in the fetus.

TEST LIMITATIONS
1. This test is designed to detect whole chromosome aneuploidies of chromosomes 13, 18, and 21 only
2. Low-level mosaicism (<20%) may not be detected by this methodology
3. Structural chromosome abnormalities and segmental imbalances will not be detected
4. Maternal cell contamination, if present, may affect results
5. This test does not screen for other genetic conditions

RECOMMENDATIONS
1. Follow-up karyotype analysis from cultured chorionic villi is recommended to confirm the diagnosis and exclude structural abnormalities
2. Genetic counselling is strongly recommended to discuss:
   - The implications of trisomy 21/Down syndrome
   - Recurrence risks for future pregnancies
   - Available management options
   - Additional testing considerations

Reported by: [redacted name], Clinical Scientist
Authorized by: Dr. [redacted name], Consultant Clinical Geneticist
Report Date: [redacted date]
